messages:
maria: FYI SIEM is spamming with ~400 hits for `internal_api_key_spike` since 03:00 UTC. Looks like most are from our auth-service when it rotates service keys. Thinking we should tighten the rule to correlate with KMS/audit events instead of blind rate thresholds.

kevin: Ugh, saw that. The rotation burst is expected from the new rollout. We should add an allowlist for keys rotated by auth-pipeline (tagged) and lower the sensitivity.

olga: Can we tag service accounts at creation time? If auth-service sets metadata "rotated_by=auth-pipeline" we can exclude those in detection. Otherwise we'll keep tuning forever.

sam: Strong :+1: to correlation rather than allowlist if possible. We still need a fallback to catch real enumeration attempts — maybe require both high rate AND no matching KMS audit event in the last 5m.

anita: Agreed. Also we should avoid whitelisting IPs. Attackers can proxy. Suggest: 1) correlate with KMS audit log (RotateKey/UpdateKey) 2) require unusual credential usage pattern (new IP / cross-region) 3) score anomalies instead of hard drop.

maria: Draft of proposed change (Sigma-like):
```
title: Internal API key spike - v2
detection:
  selection:
    event.action: ["api.request"]
    credential.type: "service_account_key"
  condition: selection | count by credential.id where count > 50 in 5m
  filters:
    - not exists cloud.audit.event where cloud.audit.event.action in ("kms.RotateKey","kms.CreateKeyVersion") and timestamp >= credential.rotate_ts - 300s
  tagging: enrich credential.id -> inventory.service_account.tagged_rotated_by
  score: add anomaly_score(ip, user_agent)
```

maria: If we can enrich with `inventory.service_account.tagged_rotated_by == auth-pipeline` then we can reduce noise a lot.

kevin: Looks good. Two notes: 1) Our KMS logs live in a different index with 3m ingestion lag sometimes. We should query a separate pipeline or accept 3m TTL. 2) Add a metric to track how many alerts get suppressed vs. correlated.

josh: I can update the rule and add a suppression metric on the dashboard. I'll push to staging tomorrow and run a backfill test.

anita: Also add a short-lived suppression window (10m) and create a ticket to audit all tagged service accounts weekly. If the suppression hides a real incident, having the audit will help.

sam: We should also log an audit event when suppression happens: "siem.suppressed_by_correlation" with reason and raw_count. That way our post-incident queries can find suppressed incidents.

maria: Good call. Add a field to the alert payload: `suppression_reason` and `correlation_hits`.

josh: Plan: 1) add enrichment pipeline to tag rotated keys 2) update Sigma rule to require KMS correlation or higher anomaly score 3) add suppression audit event + dashboard metric 4) deploy to staging Wed 09:00 UTC, monitor 24h, then prod if noise drops.

deploy-bot: rule-update/api_key_anom_v2 deployed to staging by josh at 2026-03-25T09:02:13Z :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: @oncall pager duty notify (eng-sre) for any escalations during staging window.
